newsitem.title: UK: London gold loses ground at afternoon fixing.
newsitem.headline: London gold loses ground at afternoon fixing.

text.p: Gold prices were testing lower levels later on Friday after a ruminative morning in Europe, dealers said.

Dealers said thoughts centered on statements from the Swiss National Bank and the Swiss Finance Ministry on selling gold from reserves to support a Holocaust memorial fund and other causes from the profits of revalued Swiss gold reserves.
As far as the gold market was concerned, this was the "thick end of the wedge", according to market analyst Tony Warwick-Ching at CRU International.

The rethinking by the Swiss, hitherto seen as one of the most pro-gold governments in the world, was "of the highest importance to the gold market," he said as the market came to terms with the significance of the Swiss issue.
Gold was fixed at $350.30 on Friday afternoon down from $351.70 in the morning.
New York's Comex April futures contract was printed $350.60 down $3.00 at 1600 GMT.
U.S. February employment data showed a non-farm payroll rise of 339,000 in February against 247,000 in January and the jobless rate falling to 5.3 percent from 5.4 percent.
Analyts had been looking for a rise in payrolls of 230,000 jobs in February.
The data set the dollar up for a run against European currencies which was shortlived but still held the U.S. currency close to the day's highs by mid-afternoon.
Dealers and analysts had forecast a test of support at $350.00 with the possibility of a test of the mid $340s, although that looked unlikely today.
Nevertheless, medium term it could attract renewed producer selling from miners who had set aside sell orders as gold came up from its mid February low of $336 to last week's high of around $363.00.
Technically there was a chance of gold rising to fill a gap on the April Comex chart between $357.70 and $360.10.
But dealers said the market probably lacked the confidence to go for that target.
"The technicals are turning towards further declines," one dealer said.
Silver was quoted barely changed at $5.18/$5.20 but could dip to $5.12/$5.14 if gold values fell, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium were unchanged at $380.50/$381.50 and $148.00/$149.00.
